prompt.context_jp: 東京・新宿の高層ビル群の上に、春の気配をわずかに含んだ空___広がっていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 空___広がっていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle. The sky is newly introduced into the scene.

feedback.correct_en: This is a scene-setting description introducing the sky as new information in the narrative — が marks the newly observed subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn 空 into a known topic, which doesn't fit this opening descriptive line. を would require a transitive verb.

contrast_examples.en: The sky was spreading out (newly described).
As for the sky, it was blue (topic).

prompt.context_jp: テーコー不動産新宿営業所には、海辺の町から戻って来た一人の女___いる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 一人の女___いる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle. A new character is being introduced.

feedback.correct_en: Existential 'there is a woman' introduces a new referent — が is required.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose that this woman is already a known topic, which contradicts the introductory framing.

contrast_examples.en: As for the woman, she is there (presupposes her).

prompt.context_jp: 業界全体が低迷する中、本部___売り上げの数字にますます目を光らせている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 本部___売り上げの数字にますます目を光らせている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle. 本部 is the sentence's established topic being commented on.

feedback.correct_en: 本部 is a known entity being characterized — は marks it as the topic for commentary.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would signal new/exhaustive information, but here 本部 is the familiar backdrop whose behavior is being described.

contrast_examples.jp: 本部は目を光らせている。

prompt.context_jp: 残業___減らせ 売り上げ___上げろ って矛盾してませんか？
prompt.prompt_jp: 残業は減らせ、売り上げ___上げろ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 売り上げ in this contrastive pairing.

feedback.correct_en: The speaker is contrasting two opposing demands (overtime vs. sales). Contrastive は highlights the pair.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark new info and lose the contrastive pairing. も would mean 'also,' which contradicts the opposition.

contrast_examples.jp: 残業は減らせ、売り上げは上げろ。

prompt.context_jp: 家のローン___だいぶ前に払い終えました。
prompt.prompt_jp: 家のローン___だいぶ前に払い終えました。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle. The loan is the topic of commentary.

feedback.correct_en: The speaker is giving a status update about his loan — a familiar topic framed with は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce the loan as new, but he's elaborating on his own known financial situation.

contrast_examples.en: The loan — I've paid it off (topic).

prompt.context_jp: 去年 結婚しました娘___家が欲しいと言い出したので
prompt.prompt_jp: 娘___家が欲しいと言い出した
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in the subordinate clause introducing the daughter's request.

feedback.correct_en: In a subordinate clause introducing a new event ('my daughter started saying...'), が marks the clause-internal subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は tends to scope over the main clause as a topic, which doesn't fit this embedded 'because' clause.

contrast_examples.en: Because my daughter brought it up

prompt.context_jp: うちの娘___計画性がなくて 見ておれないのですよ。
prompt.prompt_jp: うちの娘___計画性がなくて
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle. The father is commenting about his daughter.

feedback.correct_en: The father makes his daughter the topic to describe her character trait — classic は for commentary.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would signal exhaustive identification ('it's my daughter who...'), which isn't the point.

contrast_examples.en: My daughter has no foresight (topic + comment).
It's my daughter who's at fault.

prompt.context_jp: 私に売れない家___ありません！
prompt.prompt_jp: 私に売れない家___ありません！
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle. Machi declares there is no such house.

feedback.correct_en: With ない predicates, Japanese strongly prefers は for the subject of negative existence — her signature line uses contrastive-emphatic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound flat and ungrammatical here; the negative existential pattern X はない is idiomatic.

contrast_examples.en: There is no house I can't sell.
There's no one who'll buy (plain neg existence with が also possible, but は emphasizes).

prompt.context_jp: 娘夫婦の暮らしと父親の思惑、その両方を満たす家___探すのは容易ではない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 両方を満たす家___探すのは容易ではない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the direct object of 探す.

feedback.correct_en: 探す is a transitive verb; its object (the house to find) takes を.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn 家 into the subject of 探す, which doesn't fit the meaning.

prompt.context_jp: 彼女___帰って来る場所があるという事実は、屋代にとって何よりの支えだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女___帰って来る場所がある
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in this relative clause.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a relative clause modifying 場所, the subject takes が (は is blocked in most relative clauses).
feedback.incorrect_en: は in a relative clause here would sound ungrammatical because topic marking generally doesn't scope inside noun-modifying clauses.

prompt.context_jp: 仕事を終えた万智の前に、留守堂謙治___ふらりと姿を現した。
prompt.prompt_jp: 留守堂謙治___ふらりと姿を現した。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle. Rusudo appears suddenly on the scene.

feedback.correct_en: A character appearing on scene is prototypical new-information — が marks the appearing subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose Rusudo as a known topic and defuse the surprise of his sudden entrance.

prompt.context_jp: 課長___愛しているからです。
prompt.prompt_jp: 課長___愛しているからです。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the object of 愛する.

feedback.correct_en: 愛する is transitive; the beloved is marked with を.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make Section Chief the one doing the loving, flipping the meaning.

prompt.context_jp: ところが万智が戻って来てからというもの、その座___揺らぎ続けている。
prompt.prompt_jp: その座___揺らぎ続けている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle. Adachi's position (the topic) is what's being commented on.

feedback.correct_en: その座 refers back to Adachi's established 'ace' position — は carries this known topic into a new comment.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would re-introduce it as new, but it was just discussed in the prior sentence.

contrast_examples.jp: その座は揺らいでいる。

prompt.context_jp: 1か月の総労働時間を 190時間に___ようにと 本部から言われました。
prompt.prompt_jp: 190時間に___ようにと
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the verb used by HQ's directive.

feedback.correct_en: 〜にする expresses a deliberate decision/policy — fitting HQ's active directive to cap hours at 190.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜になる would imply the hours spontaneously becoming that, not a company policy decision.

contrast_examples.en: It becomes 190 hours (happens on its own).

prompt.context_jp: ___。 いくつか物件をそろえて ご連絡いたします。
prompt.prompt_jp: ___。 いくつか物件をそろえて ご連絡いたします。
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in Machi's formal acknowledgment to the client.

feedback.correct_en: 承知いたしました is the humble business-polite acknowledgment appropriate for responding to a client.
feedback.incorrect_en: 分かった is casual peer-level speech. 大丈夫です is too informal and doesn't signal acceptance of a request.

prompt.context_jp: 僕だって___なんだよ。人事と営業の両方から別々に呼び出されて...
prompt.prompt_jp: 僕だって___なんだよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the idiom describing Yashiro's position caught between two sides.

feedback.correct_en: 板挟み (literally 'squeezed between boards') means being caught between two conflicting pressures — exactly Yashiro's situation between HR and sales.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手遅れ means 'too late'; 見返り means 'reward/return'. Neither captures the between-two-sides nuance.

prompt.context_jp: (庭野が鍵村に教えに行ったはずなのに、庭野の方が影響されてしまった場面で)
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the idiom describing someone who went to persuade and ended up persuaded.

feedback.correct_en: ミイラ取りがミイラになる means the mummy-hunter became a mummy — the one meant to influence got influenced instead. Fits Niwano being swayed by Kagimura.
feedback.incorrect_en: 猫の手も借りたい means desperate for any help. 石の上にも三年 is about perseverance. Neither matches the role-reversal here.

contrast_examples.jp: ミイラ取りがミイラになる。

contrast_examples.en: I'd borrow even a cat's paw (so busy).

prompt.context_jp: (娘が親の思いを分かっていないと嘆いて)
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___」とは よくいったものだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the proverb about children not knowing their parents' hearts.

feedback.correct_en: 親の心子知らず literally 'the child doesn't know the parent's heart' — perfectly matches the father's lament here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 馬の耳に念仏 means wasted advice; 知らぬが仏 means ignorance is bliss. Neither targets the parent-child disconnect.

contrast_examples.en: Children don't know their parents' feelings.

prompt.context_jp: (万智が席を立ちながら)
prompt.prompt_jp: お客様を___に行って来ます。
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the polite word for 'greet/meet' a client.

feedback.correct_en: お出迎え means to go greet/receive an arriving guest — the correct action when a client is coming.
feedback.incorrect_en: お見送り is to see someone off (opposite direction). お届け is to deliver something.

prompt.context_jp: 夢はまず 夢を___ところから始まるんだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 夢を___ところから始まる
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the verb that collocates with 夢 here.

feedback.correct_en: 夢を見る is the fixed collocation for 'to dream/have a dream.' Niwano's phrasing plays on it.
feedback.incorrect_en: 夢をする is ungrammatical. 夢を持つ ('hold a dream') exists but doesn't fit this 'start from dreaming' construction.

prompt.context_jp: (山路からのお土産を受け取って万智が)
prompt.prompt_jp: ありがとうございます。___いたします。
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the humble verb for 'accepting/receiving' from a client.

feedback.correct_en: 頂戴いたします is a humble expression for gratefully receiving a gift — exactly the right business-polite acceptance.
feedback.incorrect_en: 拝見 means humbly 'see/look at.' ご覧 is honorific for the other party's seeing. Neither fits accepting a gift.

contrast_examples.en: I will humbly take a look.

prompt.context_jp: 留守堂に「なぜテーコーに戻ったのか」と聞かれた万智の答え。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural as Machi's punch-line reveal?

choices.text: 課長を愛しているからです。
課長が愛しているからです。
課長は愛しているからです。

feedback.correct_en: 愛する takes a direct object with を — 'because I love the Section Chief.' This matches the story's actual line.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mean the Section Chief is the lover (wrong subject). は would awkwardly topicalize him within a 'because' clause.

prompt.context_jp: 万智が山路氏に向かって決め台詞を言う場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural as Machi's signature declaration?

choices.text: 私に売れない家はありません！
私は売れない家がありません！
私で売れない家はないです！

feedback.correct_en: The idiomatic signature uses 私に (dative 'for me') + はありません to declare no such house exists for her to fail at.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option b scrambles the particles and loses the negative-existential idiom. Option c sounds informal and awkward.

contrast_examples.jp: 私に解けない問題はない。
contrast_examples.en: There is no problem I can't solve.

prompt.context_jp: 庭野が仕事の意義に迷い始めて屋代に打ち明ける場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for Niwano's reflective question?

choices.text: 家を売るという仕事は自分にとってどんな意味があるんでしょうか？
家を売るの仕事は自分にどんな意味があるのでしょう？
家を売るって仕事に自分でどんな意味があるの？

feedback.correct_en: 〜という仕事 is the natural way to nominalize 'the job of selling houses,' and 自分にとって is the standard collocation for 'to me.'
feedback.incorrect_en: Option b uses 売るの+仕事, which is ungrammatical (should be 売るという or 売る). Option c mixes casual って with awkward 自分で.

contrast_examples.jp: 自分にとって意味がある

prompt.context_jp: 万智が山路氏に予算と希望地を尋ねる場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing is the most natural business-polite request?

choices.text: まず ご予算と ご希望の場所があれば お聞かせいただけますか。
まず 予算と 希望の場所があれば 聞かせてくれますか。
まず ご予算と ご希望の場所を 聞いてもいいですか。

feedback.correct_en: お聞かせいただけますか is a classic humble request form appropriate for addressing a client, paired with ご-prefixes on 予算 and 場所.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option b drops the honorific ご and uses casual 聞かせてくれる. Option c mixes ご-nouns with the less-polite 聞いてもいいですか.

contrast_examples.jp: お聞かせいただけますか。
contrast_examples.en: Would you kindly let me hear (humble).

prompt.context_jp: 留守堂が万智の答えを受けて一人つぶやく場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version flows most naturally as Rusudo's wistful line?

choices.text: 愛する人と働くってことが一番ステキなんですね。
愛する人を働くことが一番ステキなんですね。
愛する人に働くのが一番ステキなんですね。

feedback.correct_en: 〜と働く ('work with someone') uses the comitative と. ってこと nominalizes the action naturally in spoken Japanese.
feedback.incorrect_en: を働く is ungrammatical (働く isn't transitive here). に働く would mean 'work for/toward' and doesn't fit 'work alongside.'
